public_health_question.v: What was the source of an unexpected winter cutaneous anthrax case in Texas, and how was it confirmed when culture was negative?

ev.q: An unexpected anthrax outbreak occurred during winter in a Texas county adjacent to the Anthrax Triangle
Anthrax on a Sheep Farm in Winter
On January 4, 2024, a male rancher aged 50–59 years was evaluated at hospital A
An unexpected anthrax outbreak occurred during winter in a Texas county adjacent to the Anthrax Triangle
interviews were conducted with the patient and his family members

equity.level_reason: Age and sex of the single patient are descriptors only, with no social-position framing; ranching is a route of exposure, not SES.

notes: A single-patient case report with laboratory confirmation, so data_focus is limited. ELISA and mass spectrometry confirm case status (seroconversion, LF detection) and are not recorded as procedures; the fourfold rise is an interpretive criterion, not a test. The CBC values are compared with reference ranges clinically and are not analyzed. [review] Brief rule: a lab test that only confirms case status is not a procedure; by the same logic the paired-sera rise is not treated as an analytic comparison.
view_issues: Table 1 CSV fills down the 'Clindamycin' event across the 4 January CBC rows. Text says ewe nasal swabs were taken at least 12 hours after death (6 and 11 January), but Table 1 dates the ewe swabs to 12 January. The acute anti-PA IgG is 0 μg/mL, so 'fourfold increase' is a ratio on zero and rests on the footnote's 3.7 μg/mL rule.
